[[File:Michael Riboulet 1998 Worlds portrait.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Michael Riboulet, 1998 World Championship.]]
'''Michael Riboulet''' was runner-up at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]] and the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]] (United Kingdom). He was the first player in two Grand Finals. Gary Carman later named him as a Bristol playtest partner. Riboulet qualified through Kiffex Euro GenCon from Bristol.<ref name="pkt">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf 1998 World Championship packet], Decipher / Kendrick Summers (20 November 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195330/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== 1997 World Championship statement ==

"I'm 23, and live in a small city in the west of England. I have played and collected Star Wars CCG since it came out, but have only entered one official tournament, the London Open. I play Star Wars CCG every Thursday evening at my local card gaming club. I also enjoy role-playing, live action role-playing, reading and playing Quasar."<ref name="dec97bio">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/riboulet.html Michael Riboulet], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990428071324/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/riboulet.html Internet Archive]</ref>
